title: Expand/contract data migration with no record stranded
objective: The craftbook drives an expand/contract migration of a JSON user store from a flat name field to a nested profile shape: a plan grounded in the real files, accessors changed at their real sites with the suite green between stages, the data transformed with every value surviving exactly, and the old shape fully retired - verified mechanically, including a pure-nested-record probe proving the dual-read did not linger.
prompt: Use the Schema / Type Migration craftbook for this: migrate our user records from the flat name field to the nested profile shape described in source/migration-brief.md. setup.about: A tiny user-roster module backed by a JSON data file. Tests run with `npm run test` (node --test).

files.content:
# Migration brief: nested profile shape

We sort and filter by last name now, so the flat `name` field has to go.

Current record shape in `data/users.json`:

    { "id": 1, "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com" }

Target record shape:

    { "id": 1, "profile": { "first": "Ada", "last": "Lovelace" }, "email": "ada@example.com" }

Rules:

- Every existing record must survive the migration exactly - same people, same
  emails, names split on the single space between first and last name.
- The accessors in `src/users.js` must keep working for their callers at every
  stage: `fullName` and `byFullName` keep returning the same display names as
  today.
- When the migration is done, nothing reads the flat `name` field any more.

craftbookParams.scope: Migrate data/users.json and src/users.js from the flat name field to profile.first/profile.last per source/migration-brief.md, with no record loss and reads working at every stage.

success.summary: Every record reaches the nested profile shape with its values intact, the accessors read the new shape with the dual-read retired, the flat field is gone from data and code, the suite is green, and every fleet artifact exists with honest receipts.
